newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 23.

text.p: Following are the highlights of the Irish press on Wednesday:
- The British and Irish governments are resigned to defeat in today's crunch vote on decommissioning at a plenary session of the Stormont talks.
- The pound has fallen to its lowest level against sterling in more than six years, dropping close to 88 pence as the British currency continues to surge ahead on the foreign exchange markets.
- The Department of Foreign Affairs has suspended funding of new projects for the leading Third World relief agency, Goal, following an unprecedented row over the accounts submitted by the agency.
- Police in Drogheda have confirmed they received a dangerous driving complaint about 15 minutes before a crash in which six people were killed north of the town.
- Swiss banks today invite 2,000 Holocaust account holders - including two Irish names - to claim part of an estimated $40 million fortune.

- Amid signs of divided opinions within the Protestant population, the three main unionist parties are today expected to reject the terms for wide-ranging talks laid down by the British and Irish governments.
- Police were called in yesterday by the Bank of Ireland to investigate an alleged fraud by an official at a provincial bank branch which could involve up to one million punts.
- Public Enterprise Minister Mary O'Rourke will report to the cabinet on Monday on intensive talks held with CIE management and unions last night in a bid to avert a national transport strike.
- The headquarters of the Veronica Guerin murder investigation was "bugged", the High Court heard yesterday.

- Paedophile priest Brendan Smyth yesterday publicly apologised for his sexual offences which he described as "sins against God, offences against individual persons and offences against the laws of the state".
